question: The colour of the alluvial soils varies from _________.
solution:
The correct answer is__** light grey to ash grey.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **colour of alluvial soils **varies from **light grey to ash grey.**
 
• This is because alluvial soils are formed by the deposition of sediments brought by **rivers and streams,** which are usually **light in colour.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alluvial soils** are generally** fertile and rich in nutrients**, making them ideal for agriculture.
 
• They are found in **river valleys and deltas, **and are especially important for **rice cultivation.**
 
• It is important to note that the colour of alluvial soils can vary** depending on the region** and the **type of sediment** that is deposited.
 
• In some areas, alluvial soils may be** darker in colour** due to the presence of **organic matter or minerals.**

 [IMAGE: https://www.vedantu.com/question-sets/044ca21e-fea3-4f13-ab5d-583474e4cf7c3069483307916240131.png]
